title: Oatcakes with butter beans and celery

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, flour, tinned butter beans, tahini, lemon and celery are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-built.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, tahini included, is an everyday item at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a baking tray, a masher and a board, and pressing and cutting a simple dough is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: The dough ratio of 200g dry to 100ml water and 3 tbsp oil holds together, 16 thin oatcakes crisp in 20 to 25 minutes at 190°C, and a tin of beans plus 3 celery sticks tops them generously for four; moving the squares to the tray is obvious to any cook.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers mixing, pressing and cutting the dough, mashing the beans and slicing the celery and parsley, and the 25 minute bake matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the oil split as 3 tbsp plus the rest, the lemon and the parsley, is used, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water and flour for the board.

seasonal_feel.reason: A crunchy celery and parsley salad piled on oatcakes is a fair October afternoon snack, and three sticks of celery with their leaves make it a real component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour would follow without trouble.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholegrain oatcakes with a bean and tahini mash and fresh celery make a filling, wholesome snack a family would happily eat again.
